blocks.caption: Figure 9.21: Negative charge carriers (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 9.21).

blocks.text: Usually, the charge carriers in a conductor are free electrons which have negative charge.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text:
• Flow of current is directly proportional to the potential difference.
• Flow of heat is directly proportional to the temperature difference.
• Flow of fluid is directly proportional to the pressure difference.

blocks.title: For Your Information
blocks.text: Current is a flow of charge, pressured into motion by voltage and hampered by resistance.

blocks.title: Example 9.6
blocks.problem: A copper wire has a cross-sectional area of 2 × 10⁻⁶ m² and carries a current of 3 A. If the number of elections per unit volume is 8.5 × 10²⁸ m⁻³, calculate the drift velocity of the electrons in the wire. Charge on an electron is 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book numbers this example 9.6 a second time (the electron-volt example in 9.6 already has that number); it should have its own number. The working is right: v = 3/(2 × 10⁻⁶ × 8.5 × 10²⁸ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 1.1 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹. (“elections” is a misprint for electrons.)
